vocabulary.example: Twist the lid to open the jar.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone agree to do something
vocabulary.example: He persuaded me to stay longer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to pull something quickly and hard
vocabulary.example: The child tugged at her mother's sleeve.

vocabulary.meaning_en: your deepest feelings of love and sadness
vocabulary.example: The film pulled at my heartstrings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the part of the body between the head and shoulders
vocabulary.example: She wore a scarf around her neck.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an area with many trees, smaller than a forest
vocabulary.example: We went for a walk in the woods.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a part of a town or country
vocabulary.example: Is there a pharmacy in this area?

vocabulary.meaning_en: clothes that need washing or have been washed
vocabulary.example: I do the laundry on Saturdays.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move on hands and knees; (insects) to move slowly
vocabulary.example: The baby is learning to crawl.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a strong feeling of dislike for something unpleasant
vocabulary.example: He looked at the dirty kitchen with disgust.

vocabulary.meaning_en: moving in a careless way and often breaking things
vocabulary.example: I'm so clumsy – I dropped my phone again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long thin stick of wood or metal
vocabulary.example: He uses a long rod for fishing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to offer to do something without being asked or paid
vocabulary.example: She volunteered to clean the classroom.

fine_lines.title: twist someone's arm vs tug at the heartstrings
fine_lines.explanation_ar: twist someone's arm = تُقنع شخصاً بفعل شيء لا يريده في البداية (غالباً بمزاح: OK, you've twisted my arm). tug/pull at the heartstrings = يحرّك مشاعر قوية من الحزن أو الحب أو التعاطف.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Twist someone's arm' = persuade someone to do something they didn't want to at first (often as a joke: OK, you've twisted my arm). 'Tug (or pull) at the heartstrings' = make you feel strong emotions like sadness or sympathy.

examples.sentence: Another piece of cake? Well, if you twist my arm...
The story of the lost dog tugged at my heartstrings.

fine_lines.title: dip your toe into vs make a rod for your own back
words: make a rod for your own back
fine_lines.explanation_ar: dip your toe into something = تبدأ شيئاً جديداً ببطء وحذر لتجربته. make a rod for your own back = تفعل شيئاً سيسبب لك مشاكل لاحقاً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Dip your toe into something' = start something new slowly and carefully. 'Make a rod for your own back' = do something that will cause you problems later.

examples.sentence: I'm dipping my toe into online selling.

examples.word: make a rod for your own back
examples.sentence: If you do his homework once, you'll make a rod for your own back.

fine_lines.title: up to my eyes in vs ham-fisted
fine_lines.explanation_ar: up to my eyes in something = مشغول جداً بشيء كثير (عمل، رسائل، غسيل). ham-fisted = أخرق، يتعامل مع الأشياء أو المواقف بطريقة غير ماهرة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Up to my eyes in something' = extremely busy with a lot of something (work, emails, laundry). 'Ham-fisted' = clumsy; doing things in an unskilful way.

examples.sentence: I'm up to my eyes in homework this week.
My ham-fisted attempt to fix the chair broke it completely.

expressions.meaning_ar: يُقنع شخصاً بفعل شيء لم يكن يريده
expressions.meaning_en: to persuade someone to do something they didn't want to do
expressions.example: I didn't want to go, but my friend twisted my arm.

expressions.meaning_en: to make someone feel strong emotions such as sadness or sympathy
expressions.example: The photo of the old couple tugged at my heartstrings.

expressions.meaning_en: to make you feel love or tenderness
expressions.example: The puppy's little face melted my heart.
I'll be in your neck of the woods tomorrow – shall we meet?

expressions.meaning_ar: مشغول جداً بكمية كبيرة من شيء
expressions.meaning_en: very busy with a lot of something stressful or time-consuming
expressions.example: I'm up to my eyes in emails today.

expressions.meaning_en: to make you feel disgusted or afraid
expressions.example: The sound of insects in the dark makes my skin crawl.

expressions.meaning_ar: أخرق، غير ماهر في التعامل مع الأشياء أو المواقف
expressions.meaning_en: clumsy; doing things in an unskilful way
expressions.example: His ham-fisted attempt to help only made things worse.

expressions.meaning_en: to start something new slowly and carefully
expressions.example: She's dipping her toe into gardening with a few small plants.

expressions.phrase: make a rod for your own back
expressions.meaning_ar: يفعل شيئاً سيسبب له مشاكل لاحقاً
expressions.meaning_en: to do something that will cause you problems in the future
expressions.example: Saying yes to every extra task is making a rod for your own back.

grammar.title: Changing the possessive: my / your / his / her
grammar.explanation_ar: في هذه التعابير يتغيّر الضمير حسب الشخص: I'm up to my eyes in work / She's up to her eyes in work. It makes my skin crawl / It makes his skin crawl. You make a rod for your own back / They make a rod for their own back.
grammar.explanation_en: In these idioms the possessive changes with the person: I'm up to my eyes in work / She's up to her eyes in work. It makes my skin crawl / his skin crawl. They make a rod for their own back.
examples: She's up to her eyes in work.
Spiders make my brother's skin crawl.
They made a rod for their own back.
